title: Set Cover by Cyclic Rotations Is NP-Complete
summary: Given an explicitly listed binary pattern of positive length $n$ and a nonnegative integer $b$ in binary, can at most $b$ cyclic rotations of the pattern cover all $n$ positions? We prove that this decision problem is NP-complete. The reduction constructs a pattern in a cyclic group of polynomial order and outputs its entire indicator word. Its principal ingredient is a replicated-marker construction: a cover within the budget must choose one translate in every layer, and each failed difference constraint leaves a block of more holes than the remaining translates can cover.
